subject: Audio analysis for a Marine Ecology project

messages.author: f490d7e718b5b755
messages.subject: Audio analysis for a Marine Ecology project
parts:
I'm not sure if this is the best place to ask for help, but I thought
I'd give it a try.

I'm looking for an easy way to quantify both the average amplitude and
average frequency of a section from an audio (wav) file. I've been
playing around with seewave, as well as with tuneR and sound, but to
be honest I'm not that familiar with R and I haven't had much luck.
There's an awesome compliment of functions in seewave, and I'm just
having trouble sorting through them (I'm not really familiar with the
physics of sound, as I'm a Marine BIologist).

So, in short, is there an easy way to get the amplitude or frequency
of a section of an imported wav file? Also, is there a way to
calculate the change in frequency/amplitude over time?

Thanks!

-Dave

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Audio analysis for a Marine Ecology project
parts:
Dear Dave,

o To get the average amplitude:
# first read your sample with readWave()
library(seewave)
library(tuneR)
a <- readWave("dave.wav")
# then you can compute the root-mean-square of the absolute values of
your sample (ie the absolute envelope)
amp <- rms(abs(a@left))
# then you need to have some calibration reference to convert it in dB SPL

o I don't understand exactly what you mean by average frequency, but
here is the way to get the average spectrum of your sample
freq <- meanspec(a)
# you can get the maximum peak or more using fpeaks():
fpeaks(freq)

HTH

Best

Jerome
